A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Peri-LN study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Transformer pre-training, instruction-tuning, benchmark evaluations, and activation/gradient analyses, including per-seed results in Appendix H.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds normalization-placement, initialization, weight-decay, optimizer, and activation-range experiments.

M1.justification: The core Peri-LN residual update is unchanged. Appendix G.7 adds a combined Peri-LN+QK-Norm variant using LayerNorm, distinct from the OLMo2-style alternative already evaluated in v1. Calling embedding normalization optional reflects an option already tested in v1.

E1.justification: Training, instruction-tuning, benchmark, C4, and Wikitext coverage is retained. v3 identifies RedPajama-Data-1T as the source for the existing representation analysis, whose plots are reused; this documents retained evidence rather than establishing new coverage. The added ablations vary model and training settings, not tasks or domains.

E2.justification: Appendix G.6 adds A+C and B-only normalization configurations to a comparison with Peri-LN and Post-LN; G.7 adds Peri-LN+QK-Norm. These are focused comparator additions. The original Pre-LN, Post-LN, and OLMo2-style comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The original benchmark protocol is retained, but v3 adds substantial experimental designs: controlled weight-decay and initialization sweeps, SGD learning-rate sweeps, and additional normalization configurations. Appendix G.8 specifies 400M models trained on 30B tokens and 100 samples for the new forward-statistics analyses. G.7 also changes the combined QK variant's normalizer to LayerNorm.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4, 6–7 and Appendices G/I add targeted instability diagnostics, final-layer gradient tracking, weight-decay and initialization interventions, alternative placements, QK augmentation, SGD checks, and an FP16-range analysis. These substantially extend tests of the proposed stability mechanism. The original representation and embedding-normalization analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report five pre-training seeds, benchmark means and standard deviations, individual-seed tables, and exclusion of diverged checkpoints. Additional individual-run plots and stronger wording about seed coverage do not establish increased repetitions or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v1 Table 2 and v3 Table 1 match numerically, as do all six detailed benchmark tables. v3 nevertheless adds substantial results: Table 5 reports losses of 3.01 for A+C, 3.05 for Post-LN, 2.91 for Peri-LN, and divergence for B-only; Tables 6–9 and the new SGD and precision figures add further findings under additional conditions.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix C explicitly assumes a positive RMSNorm scale gamma, an assumption unstated in v1 Appendix D. The gradient formulas and proofs otherwise remain essentially unchanged. The Post-LN bound is relocated to Appendix B, and numbering the existing variance recurrence does not introduce new mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions position Peri-LN as a unifying description of existing normalization layouts and claim improved activation control, gradient behavior, and training stability through 3.2B parameters. The revised abstract, shorter contribution bullets, and conclusion retain this central scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v3 develops a stronger variance-driven explanation of early instability and interprets weight decay and initialization as interventions on that mechanism. It adds implications for FP16/BF16, hardware, quantization, and OPT instability. Appendix B also replaces v1's huge-residual explanation of Post-LN suppression with an emphasis on depth and comparatively moderate activations.

D1.justification: v3 discloses the baseline initialization parameter of 0.02 in Table 2 and specifies 256 RedPajama samples for the retained representation analysis. It also supplies settings for the new ablations, including their forward-statistics sample count. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the original training setup.

R1.justification: Appendix A newly acknowledges Ding et al.'s Sandwich-LN precedent, and v3 adds Gemma 3 and supporting initialization, optimizer, and quantization literature. These refine prior-art attribution and broaden context while retaining the paper's positioning as an analytical and empirical study of existing normalization designs.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: v1's systematic-analysis subsection becomes a reordered standalone section, followed by separate Ablation Study and Implications sections. The abstract and contribution list are rewritten, theoretical exposition is expanded, and proofs, settings, and representation discussion are reorganized across appendices.

P2.justification: v3 adds new instability, intervention, SGD, and precision plots and several ablation tables, while removing v1's intuitive comparison table. The full representation figure moves to Appendix L with selected panels repeated in the main text; retained plots are resized and captions revised. Some new appendix plots are tightly packed, with overlaps on page 29.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the central stability argument through controlled weight-decay and initialization interventions absent from v1, complemented by placement and optimizer checks. These address important uncertainty about dependence on training choices, rather than merely adding benchmark scores. Prior-art attribution and reproducibility details also improve. The new precision discussion overreaches its activation-range measurements, and its onset-time claim conflicts with Figure 11's axis, but these localized weaknesses do not outweigh the stronger evidence for the paper's main argument.
